# Omnichannel Fashion, and What Wholesale, Dropship, and Marketplace Models Require


By[Victoria London](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/victoria-london) , *Content Writer*


Last Updated August 24, 2026


8 min read


In this article, learn about:


-


- The five questions that distinguish ecommerce models.


What dropship requires from fashion suppliers.


How retailer marketplaces such as Nordstrom and Macy’s affect inventory, fulfillment, and customer service.


Why managing multiple channels increases demands on the same[electronic data interchange (EDI) and fulfillment infrastructure](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/fulfillment/edi/) .


A retailer invitation to join its marketplace or launch a dropship program can create a new sales opportunity, while also introducing operational requirements that may not be obvious at first. For fashion suppliers, those requirements can be especially significant because size and color combinations increase stock-keeping unit (SKU) counts, fit affects returns, and trend cycles can shorten already-tight fulfillment timelines.


The differences in each model affect how a supplier manages inventory, orders, fulfillment, returns, and customer service.


## What Defines an Ecommerce Model?


Traditional wholesale to a retailer’s ecommerce site is the baseline many suppliers already understand. The retailer buys and owns the inventory, owns the customer relationship, and sets the price. The supplier provides accurate item information and delivers inventory according to the retailer’s requirements.


Other ecommerce models shift one or more of those responsibilities.

For many fashion suppliers, dropship is one of the first models that introduces a significant operational change.


## What Does Dropship Require From a Supplier?


In dropship, the retailer continues to merchandise and sell the product on its own site, but the supplier owns the inventory and ships individual consumer orders directly. The supplier must follow the retailer’s requirements for turnaround times, packaging, and other fulfillment standards.


Wholesale typically involves purchase orders delivered in batches. Dropship generates individual consumer orders, and each order requires the appropriate shipping and invoice documentation. The retailer also relies on the supplier’s inventory feed to determine whether a particular size and color combination is available.


Fashion makes inventory accuracy particularly important, as a single style can have[dozens of size and color combinations](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/upc-gtin-and-style-number-basics-for-apparel-and-footwear) . An aggregate inventory count may look healthy while one specific combination is already out of stock. If the retailer’s system still shows that item as available, the supplier may face a canceled order, a service-level penalty, or both.


Suppliers that manage dropship effectively connect order-level EDI with real-time inventory synchronization. When a sale occurs in one channel, the available inventory can be updated across other channels. This helps the supplier maintain a consistent view of inventory as orders move through different sales channels.


**Related Reading:**[Managing Online Dropship Vendor Inventory](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/managing-online-dropship-vendor-inventory)


## What Changes When a Retailer Operates a Marketplace?


Retailer marketplaces introduce another change: the supplier typically becomes the seller of record. Instead of the retailer purchasing the inventory through a traditional wholesale model, the supplier sells its products through the retailer’s website, usually pays a commission, and may control pricing and fulfillment.


### Nordstrom and Macy’s as Marketplace Examples


[Nordstrom launched a Mirakl-powered marketplace in 2024](https://wwd.com/business-news/retail/nordstrom-launches-online-marketplace-offerings-of-brands-sizes-and-prices-to-grow-1236337054/) to expand its assortment beyond what its own buying budget could support. Macy’s also operates a Mirakl marketplace, which[launched with 400 brands across roughly 20 categories](https://www.modernretail.co/technology/macys-is-the-latest-department-store-chain-to-test-out-a-third-party-marketplace/) .


Macy’s marketplace sellers fulfill their own orders. A[Mirakl case study](https://www.mirakl.com/resources/macys-case-study) reported that 90% of Macy’s marketplace customers cross-shop between Macy’s-owned and marketplace products, while a Macy’s-owned product appeared in 96% of marketplace transactions. Because those figures come from the vendor involved in the marketplace implementation, they should be treated as vendor-reported results rather than independent measurements.


For suppliers, the more important consideration is how marketplace requirements affect daily operations. The same retailer may operate wholesale, dropship, and marketplace programs, with different requirements and margin structures for each.


Marketplace sellers must also meet the retailer’s content and performance standards. Failure to meet those standards can affect a seller’s marketplace status. Amazon operates under a similar general model but has its own requirements and enforcement processes, particularly around product identifiers.


## Why Is TikTok Shop a Different Kind of Channel?


Social commerce, including TikTok Shop, introduces another operating model for fashion suppliers. Instead of relying primarily on retailer merchandising or marketplace search, TikTok Shop uses creator content, affiliate activity, and live shopping to drive demand.


Sales from[TikTok Shop brands](https://www.modernretail.co/technology/sales-from-major-brands-on-tiktok-shop-nearly-doubled-in-2025-drawing-ulta-and-sally-beauty/) with at least $30 million in annual sales increased 97% year over year in 2025, while total transaction volume increased by nearly 80%. TikTok Shop also reported more than 103 billion U.S. searches with ecommerce intent. These figures illustrate the scale of the channel, although any third-party estimates should be treated as directional.


The operating requirements can change quickly when content drives a sudden increase in demand. Inventory needs to support the resulting order volume, product listings need to remain accurate, and product information about fit can affect the customer’s expectations before the order ships.


[PUMA’s UK team reported a 737% increase in gross merchandise value during one week tied to a live-shopping and affiliate campaign](https://influencermarketinghub.com/tiktok-shop-campaigns-fashion-apparel/) . Results from individual campaigns will vary, but the example illustrates the operational challenge: demand can change quickly when social content gains traction.


For fashion suppliers, the same disciplines that support dropship can also support social commerce. Accurate item information and timely inventory updates help suppliers respond when demand changes quickly.


**Related Reading:**[TikTok Shop: How to Prepare for Viral Demand](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/tiktok-shop-how-to-prepare-for-viral-demand)


## How Do Multiple Ecommerce Models Affect Operations?


Direct-to-consumer (DTC) used to be viewed as an alternative to wholesale. For many brands, the practical question today is more complicated. A brand may operate a DTC site while also selling through wholesale, dropship, marketplaces, or social commerce.


That creates an operational challenge because each channel can rely on the same underlying inventory and product information while imposing different requirements.


A supplier running wholesale, dropship, a marketplace, and TikTok Shop is managing one inventory and content operation across four sets of channel requirements. An inventory or item-data problem in one system can affect orders in another.


The more channels a supplier adds, the more important it becomes to understand what each model requires before committing to it.


**Related Reading:**[First Steps to Omnichannel Assortments](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/first-step-to-omnichannel-assortments-complete-item-data)


## What Should Suppliers Evaluate Before Adding a Channel?


The five questions above provide a starting point for evaluating any new ecommerce model:


1. Who owns the inventory?


2. Who sets the price?


3. Who owns the customer relationship?


4. Who handles returns?


5. What does the model require from the supplier’s systems?


One additional question matters: Can the supplier’s current systems support the channel’s requirements?


For example, a supplier considering dropship or marketplace selling should understand whether its inventory feeds can update across existing channels and whether its systems can generate order-level shipping and invoice documentation without manual entry.


Connecting real-time inventory feeds and order-level EDI can help suppliers support multiple channels without rebuilding their integrations for each new trading relationship.


**Related Reading:**[How The Best Breakout DTC Brands Prepared for the Jump to Walmart and Target](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-the-best-breakout-dtc-brands-prepared-for-the-jump-to-walmart-and-target)


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What’s the Difference Between Dropship and a Retailer Marketplace?


In dropship, the retailer continues to merchandise and sell the product on its own site, while the supplier owns the inventory and ships individual consumer orders according to the retailer’s requirements.


In a retailer marketplace, the supplier typically becomes the seller of record. The supplier may set its own price, fulfill the order, and pay the retailer a commission.


### Does a Fashion Brand Need to Choose One Ecommerce Model?


No. A fashion brand can use several ecommerce models at the same time, including wholesale, marketplaces, dropship, and a direct-to-consumer site.


The important consideration is whether the brand’s inventory, product data, fulfillment, and customer service operations can support the requirements of each channel.


### What Should a Brand Check Before Accepting Its First Dropship or Marketplace Invitation?


Start with inventory and order management. Determine whether inventory can update across the channels where the brand already sells and whether the business can generate order-level shipping and invoice documentation without relying on manual entry.


These capabilities can help reduce canceled orders, inventory errors, and service-level issues as the brand adds new channels.


## How Can Suppliers Support a Fashion Omnichannel Strategy?


Each ecommerce model has different requirements, but they often depend on the same underlying data and fulfillment processes.


Accurate item data, timely inventory updates, and order-level EDI can help suppliers manage those requirements across channels.
